title: BNP Paribas CFO Discusses Targets as Bond Trading Income Falls
description: Oct.30 -- BNP Paribas SA Chief Financial Officer Lars Machenil discusses targets and profitability, the operating environment in Europe and the impact of a weaker Turkish lira, Italy and Brexit on business. Machenil speaks with Bloomberg's Caroline Connan in Paris as France's biggest bank reported a 15 percent decline in fixed-income trading in the third quarter, weighing on the lender's corporate and investment banking business.

asr.full_text: Mr. Maschini, thank you so much for being with Bloomberg TV today. So first, you still see lackluster capital markets and difficulty on interest rates. How much does this weigh on your third quarter? Well, good morning. But if you look at our third quarter, honestly, if you look at the business development, BNP Paribas showed good development because if you look at the loans they're basically up 4.2 percent if you look at the bottom line the net income it's up four percent as well on the quarter compared to a year ago if you then look at the profitability the return on tangible equity 11 the same thing if you look at the balance sheet it is very strong as you can see. The Common Equity Day 1 went up 25 basis points in the quarter, 2,000 to 11.7%. So that's basically the things that we see. Of course there are some lacklustre environments in Europe on some of the activities. We compensate by deploying our resources efficiently. That's why if you look at the costs you see that the costs are picking up in the specialised businesses of retail to accompany that growth that I talked about or that they are reducing in the retail networks and in CIB to face the pressure on the top line. But you still have continued pressure when it comes to the fixed income business for example yes i mean we at the bank we are focused on the activities mainly in europe let's be fair and the fixed income in europe has been lackluster however we continue to serve clients mind or market share in those activities and ensure that we do this in a profitable way and you can you can see this. If you look at CIB as a whole, the pre-tax return on equity is clocking in at 16%, so that's fine. Your investment bank target for 2020 are increase of 4.5% of revenue growth, do you think because of this difficulty in the fixed income business is going to be more challenging to achieve them? Let's be very fair if we look at, as I said, we are to focus on helping our customers and to do this in a profitable way. Therefore what we aim to do, and which is what we have, we have a pre-tax return on equity of 16%. And that is what we want to achieve. Now, if there are moments with less or more demand, that is what we want to achieve. Now if there are moments with less or more demand, that's fine we are there to serve that demand, but the important thing for us in the focus is to do this in a profitable way and that's what we've done, that's why we have adapted the costs, that why we have adapted the capital requirements, to ensure the pre-tax return on equity will be above 16%. So today you're maintaining these targets? We aretax return on equity to be above 16%. So today you are maintaining these targets ? We are maintaining the return on equity targets as I said this is basically what we go for. We are well positioned to do that, what the overall evolutions will be and the volumes we will have to see but it's the profitability that we go for. Maintaining the profitability target but not quite sure yet about the revenue increase when it comes to CIB business. Listen if I had a crystal ball, I would tell you. But that is... for us, the main thing is we want to be there with the client demands doing that and in a profitable way, that's the focus. In France when it comes to the retail bank, how do you see the rest of the year and 2019 going forward? If you look at our French retail activities, what we see is that we accompanied the growth that our clients are needing. We also having behind us now the buybacks and the renegotiations that we had at the beginning of 2017. So we anticipate that at the end of the year we will switch to the fourth quarter and we will tilt again into the positive theory of evolution and continue that in 2019. In the fourth quarter of 2019... So, that will be the turning point for the French retail? Yes, that's what we anticipate. Are you going to close some branches in in order to achieve that in France? Listen, you are asking the elements are the top line. So in the top line we see its evolution. When it comes to cost that is really quickly what we continue to do in all our networks. Yes, in France but in Belgium and in Italy. So we optimize the layers of management, we optimize our branches and optimizing branches can mean that we change them in number of square meters a number of staff and so forth. So that is an optimisation that we continue to do. G.S. So and it is possible we will see some branch cut in France? IG. As I said in our previous plan, in the current plan, we are on the trajectory to reduce the square meters that we are offering and that is what we will continue to do. G.S. BNP, of course course also has a big unit in Italy, cold BNL. BNL revenues were at 8.3% in the 3rd quarter due to a negative impact of non-recurring items. Are you concerned about the pressure we're currently seeing from Brussels asking to revise the Italian budget? Could Italy go into trouble again? For the moment it's of course a point of attention but what we see and what we've done in the last couple of years, we focused in Italy let's not forget in Italy our market share, you can count it on the fingers of one hand and so we've focused our activities on the core clients that BNP Paribas serves well. So it's the corporates, which are internationally interested and so forth. And so that is what we keep on doing. And so that basically means that, yes, there is some pressure on the top line, however, that is more than compensated by the impact in the cost of risk, and that's what we basically see. We see our bottom line in Italy increasing because of our continued improvement in the cost of risk. Can you update us on your Italian sovereign holdings and what you are doing to protect your balance sheet from the situation in Italy? The thing is that if you look at the combination of funding that we do in each of the countries, be it Belgium, be it France or Italy, we have a more blended way of funding that we do in each of the countries where we are, be it Belgium, be it France, be it Italy, we have a blended way of funding the balance sheet. So we have deposits. We also have then some bonds that we have. And that is a natural equilibrium where we don't push into one domain as excessive as in another, so for us our levels are at a level which is not a concern. There has been a lot of tensions with the Saudis after the death of this journalist and BNP Paribas does operate in the Saudi market even though it has a small presence. Do you have some exposure to the tensions we may see geopolitically with Saudi? No, first let's not forget, as I said, we are mainly a European bank that are active in some areas, but that's basically it. There's nothing else to mention. But still, there's been a lot of discussions that BNP being one of the banks exposed to the Saudi market. Can you just tell us little bit about this? It is not a concern. As you know, we at BNP Paribas, as I said, we are a European bank following exposure of our clients in some of these areas and that's basically what we do. But there is never a material exposure in these activities that we have. You are also one of the most exposed banks to Turkey that already weighs with Turkish Lira on your IFS unit this quarter. Is it a danger for your growth of your International Financial Services Unit in the future? If you look at Turkey's activity, there are also – let's be fair – we have an activity in Turkey, but, again, the market share you can count it on the fingers of one hand. Moreover, it is very well managed, it is very well capitalized, it is self-funded, so, actually, that activity, which is Turkish-based, is fine. The issue is, of course, the results it generates are in Turkish dirhams, and as Turkish dirhams have lowered versus the euro, basically when you include it in the balance sheet of BNP Paribas which is in euros when you compare it is indeed lower due to the evolution of the Turkish Lira not of the evolution of the activity that we have in Turkey Could this weigh though on your targets? Because the IFS unit is going to be part of your 2020 targets, but if you look at all our targets as I said One important target that we use is the return on equity. So you basically take the profit but also you take the capital and so those typically move in the same way when they are exposed to Turkish lira. Yeah, so the profit generated but also the capital are in Turkish lira. So they evolve both when it comes to the forex impact, so if you look at our profitability, that will basically not be of a concern. This month EU summit on Brexit landed very little progress. Are you ready to implement your hard Brexit contingency plans? The first thing is, as you know, are of course monitoring and following this closely, However for BNP Paribas we are have having a balanced presence in Europe. Some activities we do locally in the UK, others are being book on the continent and so forth. So, we are well balanced. So, even if and we would hope there will be clarity soon, we can wait for that and then basically adapt. And one it comes to hard Brexit on banking, whatever I hear on the UK side is that they want to have a transition period, so overall I believe that situation should be manageable, but indeed the ideal is that there is rapidly a clarification. With all the concerns and challenges we just mentioned, what is the main risk you see going forward for BNP Paribas? Not the main risk, because, yes, you've pointed to some concerns. But, intrinsically, if you look at, in that environment, BNP Paribas has been growing its lending capacity by 4 percent. So, what is important for us is that we can continue to serve the clients into their ambition and into their evolution and so that is what we will continue to do. You don't have one particular concern among whatever I just couted? No, let's be very fair. I mean, we are a diverse and balanced bank, so yes you can mention those but if you look at the impact, versus what we are as a diversified bank that is very limited. Mr. Machinylli, thank you so much for being with Bloomberg TV today. Thank you very much. Thank you.
